title: Entropy release: synchronization ops slate — May 2027 (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This is the working ops slate for the May 2027 "Entropy" release. Focus: coordinated multi-service sync (serving-runtime, router, telemetry ingestion) with minimal customer-visible impact. This file is intentionally iterative — goal is to capture the preflight checklist, explicit calendar for staggered ramps, smoke test scripts, rollback triggers, and comms playbook.

Scope of the release
- Feature surface: new prefix-caching heuristics, a routing policy update that enables per-tenant fallback routing, and a lightweight autoscaler tuning change for Dedicated.
- Services touched: serving-runtime, router, autoscaler, metrics-agent, console rollout hooks.
- Risk profile: medium (changes touch request-pathing and caching). Expect transient 5xx spikes if KV cache invalidation edge-case triggers.

Key contacts
- Release lead: Maya Chen (owner) — pager +1-555-0102
- SRE lead: Carlos Ortega — pager +1-555-0111
- Platform eng: Evelyn Park (router)
- Product PM: Jonah Rivera (release window approval)
- On-call rotation: see linked_artifacts (release duty roster)

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift)
- [ ] Branch protection: all PRs merged to release branch and green CI (runtime PR #4567 merged) — owner: Maya
- [ ] Canaries passed: unit + integ + quick-regen smoke on canary cluster (see smoke steps) — owner: Carlos
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: router fallback table validated against latest model manifest — owner: Evelyn
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: span and metric names versioned to avoid aggregation key flips — owner: SRE
- [ ] Capacity runway: Dedicated pool capacity reserved for 4x expected peak for first 30 minutes — owner: capacity-ops
- [ ] Rollback artifacts: tagged rollback image and migration revert PR created (rollback tag: entropy-2027-rollback) — owner: Maya
- [ ] Stakeholder sign-off: product + security approved release notes — owner: Jonah
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready for release-notes channel (internal) — owner: comms

Canary and ramp plan (calendar)
- Day 0: 09:00 PT — deploy images to canary cluster (canary-01). Validate smoke tests. If failure, abort.
- Day 0: 10:15 PT — open 0.5% traffic to canary via router A/B header isolation. Monitor 10m latency and 5xx.
- Day 0: 10:45 PT — if metrics stable (latency within +10% baseline, 5xx < 0.1%), move to 2% traffic.
- Day 0: 11:30 PT — 5% traffic. Hold 30m. If OK, schedule rolling deploy to a second region canary-02 (EU-west).
- Day 0: 14:00 PT — 15% traffic (cross-region), smoke on heavy embedding requests. Hold 1h.
- Day 0: 16:00 PT — 35% traffic. Validate routing fallbacks under simulated pod drain.
- Day 1: 10:00 PT — 60% traffic. If still stable, proceed to 95% by 12:00 PT.
- Day 1: 12:30 PT — 100% traffic and finalize post-rollout checklist.

Notes on traffic steering
- Use per-tenant routing key 'entropy-release' header. Do not mix with other experiments.
- For Dedicated customers, route to reserved pools until post-rollout verification complete.
- If autoscaler anomalies appear (sudden pod churn), freeze traffic ramp and scale Dedicated pool manually.

Smoke test suite (quick run on canary before ramp)
- Smoke-01: simple generation (10 short prompts) across models: sanity of prefix cache hits. Expect <5ms additional inference overhead.
- Smoke-02: long-context streaming test (2 requests, 8k tokens each) — validate KV cache warm-up and no OOM.
- Smoke-03: routing fallback test — intentionally simulate unavailable model in region and confirm automatic fallback within 300ms.
- Smoke-04: telemetry ingestion check — 100 synthetic spans and metrics verify ingested to telemetry pipeline within 60s.
- Smoke-05: console routes — verify per-tenant stats show new metric labels and no schema changes detected.

Rollback and emergency stop criteria (explicit)
- Abort / rollback if any of the following occur:
  - sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 15 minutes AND correlated to new code paths.
  - tail latency P99 > baseline P99 + 200ms for > 30 minutes.
  - KV cache memory leak causing node memory > 85% for > 10 minutes.
  - Automatic fallback fails for > 3 distinct tenants in 60 minutes.
- Rollback steps (fast):
  1) Trigger emergency freeze: post in slack #release-ops "ENTROPY ABORT" and activate pager rotation.
  2) Switch router traffic policy to previous routing table (router rollback tag: router-prev-202704).
  3) Deploy rollback images to affected regions (image tag: entropy-2027-rollback).
  4) Validate canary health and stop further rollouts.
  5) Open incident in JIRA: RELEASE-321-INC and assign to release lead.

Post-rollout verification checklist
- [ ] All metrics stable for 6 hours post-100% (latency, error, CPU, memory).
- [ ] Run full e2e regression tests against production snapshot (non-blocking) — owner: QA
- [ ] Confirm that per-tenant fallback logs show expected behavior; no >0.5% unexpected fallbacks — owner: telemetry
- [ ] Publish release notes (customer-facing) and internal debrief — owner: comms

Communications plan
- Pre-announce to internal release slack 48h before deploy with calendar and on-call list.
- External customer digest: draft and review 24h before. Only send after Product OK.
- During rollout: periodic 30m updates in #release-ops and alert channel for major events.
- Post rollout: summary + retrospective items within 72h.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: Do we need to disable a/b tests for a subset of PLG customers during ramp? (owner: product)
- Q2: Verify metric cardinality after adding new routing labels — telemetry team to run offline simulation (owner: telemetry).
- TODO: Add concrete runbook snippet for manual cache invalidation (owner: runtime team).
- TODO: Add list of edge-case tenants exempt from auto-fallback (owner: customer-success).

Appendix: quick commands
- Rollback router table (example): curl -X POST https://router-admin.prod.internal/routing/swap -d '{"tag":"router-prev-202704"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
- Force canary drain: sh ops/drain-canary.sh canary-01
- Verify KV memory: kubectl top pod -n serving-runtime | grep kv-cache

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the canary traffic shifts small and conservative this time — cache-related regressions are sneaky.
- If we see a small 503 blip, check the telemetry ingestion lagfirst (rare interaction between telemetry backpressure and router).
- Remember to hand-off to product for the customer-facing change log; don't write consumer-facing wording that mentions internal fallback heuristics.

Change log for this doc (latest edits)
- 2027-05-02 created by Maya (initial slate)
- 2027-05-04 added canary timeline and smoke tests (Carlos)
- 2027-05-07 included rollback image tags and quick commands (Evelyn)
- 2027-05-10 minor clarifications on traffic steering and open questions (Maya)

If you are reading this and have suggestions, drop notes inline or DM the release lead. This is intentionally a live doc — treat it as the single source during the release window.
